summary: Marcus confirmed (USER-001) that he raised inventory-service DB_POOL_MAX from 20 to 80 at 13:52 (CFG-502). That over-committed orders-db (610 budget vs 400 max) and starved orders-service, which caused the checkout errors. After the revert to 20 at 14:35, orders-db connections returned to 250 and checkout errors fell to 0.3% (USER-002). That is the baseline, so recovery is verified. Cause confirmed.
impact: Checkout failed from about 13:55 until the revert at 14:35. 87 tickets by 14:30 against a normal ~5/hour (CUST-001). 14 customers report being charged with no order confirmation (CUST-002), so payment and order integrity still needs reconciling. Search and browsing were unaffected (CUST-004). Impact was in all regions (CUST-005). Checkout errors are back to 0.3% (USER-002).

hypotheses.statement: CFG-502 raised inventory pool to 80/replica, exhausting orders-db connections; orders-service and inventory reservations failed, causing checkout 5xx and latency
hypotheses.reasoning: Owner confirmed the change (USER-001). Reverting it restored connections and error rate (USER-002). Payments rollback had not helped (ALR-014), and payments latency was a symptom of checkout retries.
Recovery came from the pool revert, not the payments rollback.

nextActions.action: Reconcile charged-without-order cases and release duplicate holds
Re-enable checkout payments_retry_on_timeout now that recovery is verified, if still wanted
Add PgBouncer in front of orders-db (open INC-2041 item)
Add config guardrail validating pool sizes against max_connections

openQuestions: How many customers were charged without an order, and have the holds been released or refunded? (payments/orders on-call)
Why was the pool raised to 80 without a connection budget check? (Marcus / inventory team)
